emails.job: Get the reader to open the official goal-conversions guide and understand that a signup goal would show them which sources and landing pages drive their trial signups.
emails.single_idea: Setting up a single signup goal turns your trial-signup count into a breakdown of which sources and landing pages actually produce those signups.
emails.objection: Doesn't setting up a conversion goal mean touching my site's code?
must_not_say: Any measured lift the reader should expect from installing Plausible; the published 2.65%-to-4.80% / 84% figures came from Plausible editing its own homepage, not from a customer adding the product
Assume the reader currently uses Google Analytics or any named analytics tool
Assume the reader's traffic volume or site scale
Assume the reader has a privacy, cookie or consent-compliance problem to solve
Funnels and user journeys (Business-plan features) as part of this first step
Pricing, plan tiers or the free trial as the ask

Plausible can only record a paid conversion if the owner sends it as a backend event, revenue attribution sits on the Business plan, and the ledger contains nothing about in-trial product usage or billing, so the measurement stops at.

The 2.65% to 4.80% lift (E11) came from Plausible editing its own homepage, not from installing Plausible; the product locates entry pages and drop-off steps and the owner still has to make the change and re-measure.
emails.felt_need: Free-trial signups do not convert to paid at a rate the owner considers acceptable, even after a signup surge.
emails.status_quo: They add free trials that require a payment method upfront to try to convert website visitors into paying customers.
emails.why_it_fails: A signup total with no goal attached to it can't attribute conversions back to the sources or entry pages that produced them, so landing-page changes are made without knowing which pages or sources were converting in the first place.
emails.mechanism: Set up your signup as a goal: a pageview goal on the page a visitor lands on right after signing up needs no code changes, because pageviews are collected automatically. Once it records its first conversion, the Goals section reports the number of conversions, the conversion rate, and the referrer sources and entry pages driving those conversions.
emails.next_step_decision: Whether a signup goal would show them which sources and landing pages drive their own trial signups, so they can decide to set one up.
emails.next_step_value: The official guide shows how to set up a pageview or custom-event goal and exactly what the dashboard then reports: number of conversions, conversion rate, and the referrer sources and entry pages driving them.
emails.next_step_limit: Reading the guide explains the setup and the reporting; it does not configure a goal on the reader's own site or show the reader's own numbers, and it does not establish what counts as a good conversion rate for their traffic.

events.subject: See which pages drive your trial signups
events.preview_text: A signup goal turns that rising total into a source and landing-page breakdown.
events.body:
Plausible is a web analytics dashboard, and a signup goal inside it shows you which sources and landing pages actually produce your trial signups.

A running signup total rises and falls. On its own it can't tell you which referrers or entry pages were converting — so landing-page changes get made half-blind.

Setting up a signup goal answers that. Point a **pageview goal** at the page a visitor lands on right after signing up — no code changes needed, because pageviews are collected automatically.

Once it records its first conversion, the Goals section reports the number of conversions, the conversion rate, and the referrer sources and entry pages driving them.

Our official goal-conversions guide walks through the setup and shows exactly what the dashboard reports once a goal is live.

events.message: Email 1, draft 1: "The signup count is the easy part"
events.subject: The signup count is the easy part
events.preview_text: Where those trials came from is the part a raw number won't tell you
events.body:
The signup count is the easy part.

You know how many trials started this week. Which landing pages and which sources actually produced them is the part a raw number leaves you to piece together on your own.

Plausible is a web analytics dashboard. Once you set your signup up as a goal, it shows the conversion count, the referrer sources, the entry pages driving those conversions, and the top pages people convert on.

Before you set anything up on your own site, you can see that in action. Our live demo is a public dashboard with real website traffic and **real trial-signup numbers** — not a screenshot, so you can filter it and click through the sources yourself.

It's **our site's numbers, not yours**. But it's the real thing, enough to judge whether this is the view you want for your own funnel.

events.body:
A count of this week's trial signups answers "how many." It leaves "from where" open — which sources and which landing pages actually produced them.

Plausible is a web analytics dashboard. Its documentation describes what a signup goal does: set your signup as a goal, and it tracks the conversion count, the referrer sources and entry pages driving those conversions, and the top pages people convert on.

You can see that running before you set up a thing. Our live demo is a public dashboard — the website traffic and trial-signup numbers are **visible to anyone**. Not a screenshot: filter it and click through the sources yourself.

It's our numbers, not yours — but it's live, and enough to tell whether this is the view you want before you touch your own site.
events.postscript: No account needed — the demo opens straight to the dashboard.
